title: Fire screen panel
subtitle: A large tent stitch panel for a traditional firescreen frame, worked on 13-count canvas
excerpt: A firescreen panel is the largest traditional needlepoint domestic piece. This design works a central floral urn with a foliate border in basketweave tent stitch on 13-count canvas. Finished panel size is 45 by 60 cm, sized to fit a standard antique-style firescreen frame.
sourceNotes: Floral urn motif and foliate border adapted from Weldon's Practical Needlework, Berlin work large panels series (1880s). Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746, firescreen chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), fire screen entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A freestanding adjustable frame that holds a decorative panel in front of an empty fireplace. Traditional antique-style frames take a panel of approximately 40 by 55 cm to 50 by 65 cm.

heroPrompt: A large needlepoint firescreen panel in a mahogany frame showing a floral urn and foliate border in rich Victorian colours on a dark background, standing in front of a fireplace, natural light.

content.text: A needlepoint firescreen is the most ambitious traditional domestic needlepoint project. This panel fills the
firescreen frame

with a central floral urn design and a continuous foliate border, both in basketweave tent stitch on 13-count canvas. The design area is 234 by 312 holes, finishing at 45 by 60 cm. This project is worked in stages over multiple sittings.

content.text: Palette
Rose main: DMC 815 / Anchor 43: medium garnet
Rose mid: DMC 3350 / Anchor 59: ultra dark dusty rose
Rose light: DMC 3716 / Anchor 25: very light dusty rose
Leaf dark: DMC 890 / Anchor 218: ultra dark pistachio green
Leaf mid: DMC 987 / Anchor 244: dark forest green
Leaf light: DMC 989 / Anchor 242: forest green
Urn gold: DMC 729 / Anchor 890: medium old gold
Urn shadow: DMC 680 / Anchor 901: dark old gold
Background: DMC 310 / Anchor 403: black
Stretching the canvas
A floor standing scroll frame is the standard choice for a firescreen panel. The canvas is laced or attached to the rollers and can be advanced as each section is completed.
Stitches used
Basketweave tent stitch
throughout.
Working method
Mark the design on the canvas in pencil using a 10-hole reference grid. Draw the central urn position and the four corners of the foliate border.
Work the central motif first. Complete the urn, then the roses and leaves in the arrangement above and around it. Work each colour area to completion before moving to the next.
Work the foliate border. Start at the corners, which are the most complex area, and work outward toward the centres of each side.
Fill the black background last. Work in diagonal basketweave rows, advancing across the full panel area. The background is the single largest element and accounts for most of the total thread use.
Block by dampening the complete panel and pinning it square on a large flat board with T-pins every 2 cm. Leave for 24 hours minimum.
Finishing

Lace the blocked canvas over the firescreen frame board using strong linen thread, pulling the canvas taut in both directions. Fit the board into the firescreen frame according to the frame's own instructions.
What to try next
For a coordinating piece, take one element from the firescreen design: the urn alone, or one floral cluster from the border. Work it at smaller scale to repeat the palette on a faster project.
